posts.caption:
What does Jeremiah 29:11 really mean? Jeremiah 29:11: “For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.”

It was first written to exiles in Babylon, and it came with news that the exile would last seventy years. It doesn’t promise quick relief; it reveals God’s good intentions for His people, even in a long, hard season. Save this for a season of waiting.

Jeremiah 29:11 in context, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/jeremiah-29-11-meaning

#jeremiah2911 #bibleverse #hope #advent

What kind of peace does Jesus give? John 14:27: “Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.” Jesus said this the night before the cross. His peace held even then. He doesn’t promise a trouble-free life; He promises peace in Him while trouble is still real. More Bible verses about peace, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/bible-verses-about-peace #bibleverses #peace #advent #christiantiktok

posts.caption: What is a Bible verse for peace of mind? Isaiah 26:3 is a favorite: “You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.” Perfect peace, literally “peace, peace” in Hebrew, for a mind that stays on God. Worship Room’s guide gathers Bible verses about peace: the peace Jesus gives, the peace of God that guards your heart and thoughts, and peace to rest in, with a short prayer for peace.

What to pray in the morning. Psalm 5:3: “Yahweh, in the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.” Morning prayer is as old as the Psalms: lay your requests before God and watch expectantly. A prayer for tomorrow morning: Lord, I give You this day. Guide my steps and help me notice You today. Amen. More short morning prayers, from Worship Room: worshiproom.com/guides/morning-prayer #morningprayer #prayer #bibleverse #christiantiktok

What does the Lord’s Prayer mean? The prayer Jesus taught His disciples in Matthew 6:9–13, line by line.

“Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.” Prayer starts with who God is before it turns to what we need.

“Give us today our daily bread.” A request for what we need today, not a lifetime supply.

“Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.” We receive God’s forgiveness, and we extend it to others.

Pray it slowly. Pause after each line and let it sink in. Save this for tonight.

posts.title: How to Pray Psalm 91, the Protection Psalm
posts.alt: Verse pin on a deep purple, starry galaxy background. Label: Pray · Psalm 91. Heading: How to pray Psalm 91. On a parchment card: Pray it for someone else by putting their name in: “He will cover you with his feathers. Under his wings you will take refuge. His faithfulness is your shield and rampart.” Psalm 91:4. Footer: Go deeper: Psalm 91 meaning. Worship Room, worshiproom.com.
posts.caption: How to pray Psalm 91: pray verse 2 out loud as a declaration of trust, name your fears at verses 5–6 and hand each one to God, pray verse 4 for someone else by putting their name in, and end with verse 15, God’s promise to answer and to be with you in trouble. Psalm 91 isn’t a promise that nothing bad will happen; it’s a promise that God is a refuge in danger and is with His people in trouble. Worship Room’s guide has the full text of Psalm 91 and what it means, verse by verse.
